description: Stress test: synthetic capture interleaving benign rows with a low-rate attack stream (1 attack row per 20 benign rows), preserving relative order within each source -- the closest available approximation of the brief own real session mixing normal queries with a slow low-volume exfil channel.
verdict: FAILS at the chosen operating point (k/N=0.1): 0% recall, the diluted attack stream never pushes fraction_exceeding above 0.085 in any window, short of the 0.1 threshold. A more lenient k/N=0.02 (also in the original grid) partially recovers detection (18.2% recall) but at the cost of a much higher false-alert rate on pure captures (see grid search). The window rule, as tuned, is heavily biased toward dense/pure attack sessions and does not transfer cleanly to a realistic low-rate interleaved attack -- this must be reported as a limitation, not hidden behind the pure-capture test numbers.
